title: Derived continuity for a single constructible condensed module sheaf
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and a scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] whose underlying space is noetherian (every ascending chain of open subsets stabilizes). For finite intermediate fields $E\subseteq\Omega$ [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set], put $E_T^c=p_T^*C(-,E)$ using [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. Put $\Omega_T^c=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega(S)$ consists of continuous functions on a profinite set $S$ with image in one finite intermediate field. A module sheaf is constructible if it has a finite locally closed stratification on each stratum of which it is pro-etale locally the cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules over the restricted coefficient ring. Fix a finite $E$, a constructible $E_T^c$-module sheaf $M$, and a small filtered diagram $(N_i^\bullet)$ of complexes of $E_T^c$-module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention]. Assume there is one integer $a$ such that $N_i^r=0$ for every $i$ and $r<a$. Let $N^\bullet=\varinjlim_i N_i^\bullet$ be the termwise sheaf colimit and regard these complexes and $M[0]$ in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every integer $n$, the natural map $$\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}_{E_T^c})}(M[0],N_i^\bullet[n])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\operatorname{Mod}_{E_T^c})}(M[0],N^\bullet[n])$$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups. The maps are the ones induced by the colimit cocone and are natural in $M$, in maps of the filtered diagrams, and in shifts.

source.place: module docstring, Sorried input (Hom): the assertion for locally finitely presented modules into uniformly bounded below complexes; sheaf base case only

proof.text: By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], filtered colimits of module sheaves are exact. Thus for a strict filtered diagram the termwise colimit carries objectwise quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms: its cohomology is the colimit of the kernels modulo the colimit of the images. Consequently good truncation at a common cohomological lower bound does not change the comparison being proved. Functorial K-injective resolutions exist by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; replacing a strict diagram by these resolutions likewise leaves its termwise colimit quasi-isomorphic to the original one. After computing a derived functor with these models, good truncation at a common cohomological lower bound produces functorial bounded-below representatives; those truncated representatives need not themselves be injective. We prove the slightly more flexible assertion with a common cohomological lower bound, using such representatives throughout; this includes the stipulated termwise bound. The underlying noetherian space of $T$ is quasi-compact, and every open subset is quasi-compact, so intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact and $T$ is quasi-separated. The same applies to its locally closed subschemes.

The locally free case is valid on any quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme $V$. Suppose $P$ is pro-etale locally free of finite rank. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-locally-free-derived-hom], maps from $P[0]$ into $K[n]$ are $H^nR\Gamma(V,P^\vee\otimes K)$. Tensoring by $P^\vee$ preserves the lower bound and commutes with the filtered colimit: on a trivializing cover it is a finite direct sum, and the canonical tensor-colimit map is therefore an isomorphism locally, hence globally. Apply the global-sections clause of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity] to $P^\vee\otimes K_i$. This proves the desired comparison for $P$ for every integer $n$, including negative $n$, and for arbitrary strict diagrams with a common cohomological lower bound.

For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow V$ with complementary quasi-compact open immersion $j$, use [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement] to write $i_*Ri^!K\simeq\operatorname{Cone}(K\to Rj_*j^*K)[-1]$. The map here is the adjunction unit. Pullback $j^*$ is exact and preserves sheaf colimits. By [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-qcqs-pushforward-continuity] applied to the quasi-compact quasi-separated $j$, the filtered-colimit comparison for $Rj_*j^*K_i$ is a quasi-isomorphism. In functorial complex models, a cone has degree $r$ equal to the sum of the target's degree $r$ and the source's degree $r+1$, with differential built from the unit. Termwise colimits therefore commute with this cone and its differential; exact filtered colimits preserve the quasi-isomorphisms of models by step 1. Applying $i^*$ and $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ now identifies the colimit of the $Ri^!K_i$ with $Ri^!K$ by a quasi-isomorphism. The same recollement statement gives the common lower bound $a$ for $Ri^!K_i$. Hence this new filtered diagram is an admissible second argument for the inductive assertion; no constructibility hypothesis on it has been used.

Proceed by noetherian induction on closed subspaces $V$ of $T$, with the assertion quantified over every constructible $E_V^c$-module $P$, every filtered diagram with a common cohomological lower bound, and every integer shift. The empty scheme has the zero module category, so is the base case. Let $(S_b)$ be a finite stratification as in [def-constructible-stratification]. For each $b$, the boundary $F_b=\overline{S_b}\setminus S_b$ is closed in $V$ because $S_b$ is locally closed. It has empty interior: a nonempty open contained in $F_b$ would be a nonempty relatively open subset of $\overline{S_b}$ disjoint from its dense subset $S_b$. Set $U=V\setminus\bigcup_bF_b$. This is dense open, since a finite intersection of dense open subsets is dense (intersect a nonempty open with those dense opens one at a time). Each $S_b\cap U=\overline{S_b}\cap U$ is closed in $U$, and its complement is the finite union of the other such closed pieces, so it is also open. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-lfp-local-triviality] on the noetherian strata and restrict its trivializations to these disjoint open pieces. Thus $P|_U$ is locally free of finite rank. The closed complement $Z=V\setminus U$ is proper; intersecting the strata with $Z$ gives a finite locally closed stratification and inverse image preserves their presentations, since it preserves cokernels and finite free sheaves. Thus $i^*P$ is constructible on $Z$. This uses no frontier condition on the partition and no induction on a potentially unchanged count of strata. Exact restriction and its coefficient identifications are those of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement]. If a chosen stratum has a different scheme structure from the corresponding open piece, its base change to that piece is a closed immersion with full set-theoretic support. Apply the first recollement triangle with empty open complement: restriction and closed pushforward are inverse, with the coefficient rings identified. Thus the locally free restriction is the same one on the open piece; nilpotent scheme structures are not silently identified.

Use the first triangle of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-open-closed-recollement] for $P[0]$: $j_!j^*P[0]\to P[0]\to i_*i^*P[0]\to$. For the first term the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ identifies its shifted maps into $K_i$ with those from $j^*P[0]$ into $j^*K_i$; step 2 proves their filtered continuity. For the third term $i_*\dashv Ri^!$ identifies the maps with those from $i^*P[0]$ into $Ri^!K_i$. Step 3 identifies the colimit of the latter targets with $Ri^!K$ and preserves a common lower bound. The noetherian induction hypothesis on the proper closed $Z$ therefore proves continuity for this third term for all shifts. The adjunction bijections identify these comparison arrows with the arrows induced by the original cocone.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] and its rotations to the triangle of step 5 with targets $K_i[n]$ and $K[n]$. This gives the natural long exact Hom sequences in the first argument. Take filtered colimits of the first sequences, which remain exact by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-abelian-groups-exact]. For each $n$, in the five-term window $\operatorname{Hom}(j_!j^*P,K_i[n-1])\to\operatorname{Hom}(i_*i^*P,K_i[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(P,K_i[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(j_!j^*P,K_i[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(i_*i^*P,K_i[n+1])$, the four comparisons away from the middle are isomorphisms by step 5. The middle comparison is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma]. This completes the induction, and gives the claimed map for $V=T$ and $P=M$.

The arrow proved invertible is the canonical comparison, defined on a representative $f:M[0]\to N_i[n]$ by $f\mapsto (N_i[n]\to N[n])\circ f$. Precomposition with a map of first arguments and postcomposition with a map of filtered diagrams commute with this rule by associativity of composition. Replacing $n$ by $n+t$ gives exactly the shifted cocone rule, so shifts commute as well. This proves all requested naturalities; it does not require making the chosen stratification or noetherian induction functorial.
